headline: US equity futures point to a lower open as oil rises on supply concerns ahead of jobless claims data and PepsiCo earnings
raw_text:
- S&P 500 Futures (@ES) decline 0.33%, Dow Jones Futures (@YM) fall 0.66%, Nasdaq 100 Futures (@NQ) drop 0.50%, and Russell 2000 Futures (@ER2) decline 0.85% in pre-market trading
- PepsiCo (PEP) reports Q3 earnings before the bell, with consensus estimates at $2.29 EPS and roughly $25B in revenue
- Initial jobless claims data are due at 8:30 AM ET and are in focus for labor-market and Fed-policy expectations
- Oil futures (@CL) climbed sharply overnight on supply concerns, supporting energy names while reinforcing inflation worries as bond yields remain elevated
- European equities trade lower, with the DAX (@DY) and Stoxx 50 (@EX) both down around 1% in early dealings
- Asian markets weakened overnight, with the Nikkei (@NKD) off over 1%
- No major individual pre-market stock movers with explained catalysts were highlighted in reporting from CNBC (CMCSA), Reuters (TRI) or Bloomberg
- Traders are watching for any comments from Fed Governor Christopher Waller that could influence intraday rate and equity moves
